summary: Brad Gerstner, an investor in Anthropic, argues the company has posted the fastest revenue ramp in tech history, is compute-constrained not demand-constrained, has exploding gross margins, and is likely to exit the year at $80–100B run rate; he is a buyer of shares in both Anthropic and OpenAI today.
quote: I'm a buyer of the shares today, notwithstanding all of the vibes that you describe. I think these companies are firmly on the wave.

scoreNote: Explicit buy statement; context makes clear 'these companies' refers to both Anthropic and OpenAI
summary: Brad Gerstner argues OpenAI is at peak FUD, has an incoming model (SpUD) on par with Anthropic's Mythos, and is firmly on the AI revenue wave; he says he is a buyer of OpenAI shares today despite the current negative vibes.
quote: I'm a buyer of the shares today, notwithstanding all of the vibes that you describe. I think these companies are firmly on the wave.

summary: Chamath is bullish on Anthropic's competitive execution and go-to-market momentum, calling them the current leader in coding AI, but notes the market is early, the Mythos doomsday framing is largely theater, and profitability questions remain unresolved.
quote: Anthropic is shooting the lights out right now. This is like Steph Curry going bananas from everywhere on the court. These guys are hucking threes.

summary: Sacks argues Anthropic has dominant coding market share (50%+ of coding tokens), the fastest revenue ramp ever seen at scale, and a potential flywheel where coding leadership compounds into agents dominance, though he cautions the company must avoid anti-competitive pricing behavior.
quote: Anthropic's revenue run rate is, based on what I can tell and what's been publicly released, is the fastest growing revenue run rate at scale that I think we've ever seen.

summary: Brad Gerstner notes enterprise software stocks are getting crushed (IGV down 30% YTD) as AI disrupts terminal values, and venture capitalists are crowding into frontier AI and away from traditional software.
quote: You look at the IGV stock index, down 30% year to date, down 5% today. All software stocks plummeting, right? Venture capitalists are terrified to invest money in anything other than these frontier models.

summary: Sacks thinks the market is being too pessimistic on at least some enterprise software companies — cheaper software generation doesn't necessarily destroy their moats — and suggests there are value buys among those with strong competitive positions, though differentiation will matter.
quote: I think the market's probably being a little too pessimistic with respect to at least some of these software companies... there probably are some value buys in enterprise software.

summary: Chamath argues Meta's massive compute infrastructure gives it a structural advantage in AI — its models are highly performant — and predicts Meta will seek to make AI a capital problem to outcompete leaner rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI.
quote: Meta's models today, what people's general reviews are, it's okay, but the one thing that people say is it's incredibly performant... which speaks to Meta's huge advantage. They have a massive compute infrastructure.
